rationale: Classification: definite execution, no exception. Python 3.14 static reasoning; no execution. A `def` statement is an executable binding. The first `def run` binds `run` to the -S function. `return run` then leaves the call to `make` with that object. The second `def run` comes after the return, never executes and never rebinds `run`, although it is legal syntax and `run` is a local of make either way. `make()()` calls the first `run`, which reaches `subprocess.run(["pacman", "-S", "r22-cxafterdef-live"])`. Exactly one observed host_mutation row, zero unparsed. This differs from CX5AfterReturn, which places an assignment `a = b` after the return. Here the dead binding is a second function definition with the same name, which defeats identity selection that maps names to the last top-level def in the factory body. Limits: this is exact static semantics for this text, not current-code behavior.
